docs.title: Unity Plugins
docs.text:
Unity Plugin User Guide

I. Using Unity Software

1. Open Unity Hub (if not installed, download it from the official website: https://unity.cn/releases)

2. Check whether the editor is installed (minimum supported version: 2019.1.0)

If it is not installed, click the Install Unity Editor button, and install the editor through Unity Hub or download it from the official website (URL: https://unity.cn/releases/full/2019)

3. Create a new project or open an existing project

Create a new project

After creating the project, the new project opens automatically

4. If warnings appear after opening, address them (skip this step if there are no warnings)

Click Window > Package Manager

Click Visual Studio Editor > Update to 2.0.22

After the update completes, close the dialog

5. Import the Unity plugin

Download Unity plugin version 2.3.0

mostechPlugin2.3.0.unitypackage

Drag the motionPlugin2.1.0 plugin file into Project > Assets

Click the Import button

6. Drive the full-body device

Click Assets > mostech > scenes

Click Motion Animator Scene or Motion Transforms Scene

In the Hierarchy, click MotionDriver

In Inspector > Motion Source Manager (script), enter the IP and port corresponding to those in Motion

Connect the device, then perform pose calibration

Click Run to stream real-time data

7. Drive the data glove device

Click Assets > mostech > scenes

Click Motion Hand Scene

In Inspector > Motion Source Manager (script), enter the IP and port corresponding to those in Motion

Connect the device, then perform pose calibration

Click Run to stream real-time data

8. Drive combined devices

Select the same model as for the full-body device

In Inspector > Motion Source Manager (script), enter the IP and port corresponding to those in Motion

Combine the devices in Motion, then perform pose calibration

Click Run to stream real-time data

9. Drive multiple devices

In the Hierarchy, select Mostech-Robot and copy it

In Inspector > Motion Instances, enter the corresponding number of models

Click MotionDriver, then in Inspector > Motion Instances > Element0, Element1, select the corresponding Mostech-Robot

Click Mostech-Robot, then in Inspector > Actor ID, enter different numbers

Click Mostech-Robot, then in Inspector, adjust the model position by modifying x, y, z

After performing pose calibration in Motion, click Run in Unity

10. Drive multiple models with a single device set

In the Hierarchy, select Mostech-Robot and copy it

In Inspector > Motion Instances, enter the corresponding number of models

Click MotionDriver, then in Inspector > Motion Instances > Element0, Element1, select the corresponding Mostech-Robot

Click Mostech-Robot, then in Inspector > Actor ID, enter the same number

Click Mostech-Robot, then in Inspector, adjust the model position by modifying x, y, z

After performing pose calibration in Motion, click Run in Unity

II. Using Data Broadcast in Motion Studio

1. Open Motion Studio

  1. On the home page, you can create a new project or open an existing one

3. After selecting a project, enter the capture page

4. Enable data broadcast

Click the function button in the upper-left corner > Data Broadcast

Enable BVH broadcast (the port number can be any value)

5. After data broadcast is enabled, offline data can be played back without a device connected

View the file list, then double-click a data file to play it

Play the file

After configuring the Unity IP and port, click the Play button to play back offline data

6. After data broadcast is enabled, real-time data can be played back with a device connected

Connect the receiver to the computer. When the device appears in the device list, click the Connect button to connect the device

After a successful connection, put on the straps and devices in sequence according to the prompts

Once worn, click Pose Calibration and follow the prompts to perform T-Pose, A-Pose, and OK-Pose (when a data glove device combination is used) calibration

After configuring the Unity IP and port, click the Play button to play back real-time data

docs.title: Unity Motion Capture Plugin (Data Glove + Android) Documentation
Introduction
docs.text: This document will help you use the game engine Unity 3D to obtain data glove data through this SDK and correctly drive the hand model.

docs.title: Importing the Unity Motion Capture Plugin Package into the Project
docs.text:
Motion capture glove plugin package

Plugin File Version Date Update Log mostechPlugin_Android_V1.1.0.unitypackage V1.1.0 2024-11-04 [New] 1. Supports self-developed glove devices mostechPlugin_Android_V1.0.0.unitypackage V1.0.0 2024-10-17 [New] 1. Collector glove real-time data 2. Pose calibration 3. Device details

After opening the Unity project, click Asset > Import Package > Custom Package > mostechPlugin_Android.unitypackage to add it to the Unity project.

docs.title: Plugin Package Overview
docs.text:
API Call Flow

Notes:

  • During data collection, after calling an interface such as querying the battery level to obtain a result, you need to call the data collection interface again.

  • It must be packaged into an Android device for running and debugging.

docs.title: 2.1 Scene Overview
docs.text:
In Assets > Mostech > MotionCapture_Android > Scenes you can find the example scene.

  1. GloveMotionCaptureDemo, obtains glove data to drive the hand model.

Installation package

GloveMotionCapture.apk

docs.title: 2.2 Script Overview
docs.text:
1. In Assets > Mostech > MotionCapture_Android > Scripts > Mostech_AndroidSerialPort.cs

    Everything related to the serial port, for example: glove data, battery level, etc.

  2. In Assets > Mostech > MotionCapture_Android > Scripts > Mostech_MotionDriver.cs

    Everything related to driving the hand model.

  3. In Assets > Mostech > MotionCapture_Android > Scripts > Mostech_UIManager.cs

    Everything related to the UI.

  4. In Assets > Mostech > MotionCapture_Android > Scripts > Loom.cs

    Adds events from a child thread to the main thread, avoiding errors caused by a child thread directly calling methods in the Unity main thread. Each scene must have the Loom.cs script added.

docs.title: 2.3 Script Mostech_AndroidSerialPort.cs Detailed Description
docs.text:
This script interacts with the Android serial port communication SDK. The workflow within the Android SDK is: obtain an instance > initialize resources > destroy the instance.

The connection of the glove device is controlled by the Android SDK.

docs.title: 2.4 Script Mostech_MotionDriver.cs Detailed Description
docs.text: This script drives the hand model and requires binding 16 bones for each of the left and right hands. Currently, only hand models with a fixed skeleton are supported (arbitrary skeletons will be supported in future versions).

docs.title: Model Requirements
docs.text:
1. The local coordinate system of all model bones is a left-handed coordinate system, with the x-axis pointing right, the y-axis pointing up, and the z-axis pointing forward.

  2. Each finger of the left and right hands consists of three parts: the proximal, middle, and distal segments.

  3. The initial pose Euler angle of each finger bone is (0, 0, 0).

Top view

Side view

docs.title: Special Configuration When Packaging for Android
4.1 Set the Minimum API Level
docs.text: Under Edit > Player > Other Settings, set the Minimum API Level to a version >= level 29.

docs.title: 4.2 Build as ARM64
docs.text: Under Edit > Player > Other Settings, first set Scripting Backend to IL2CPP, and then check ARM64.
